actions.description: Advance the simulated world by a bounded number of fixed timesteps, optionally applying an action for each step, and return the resulting observation and terminal flags.

inputs.description: Control steps to advance; the values are applied at every step
inputs.name: ticks

inputs.description: The control vector, shaped like VABEnv.step's action
inputs.name: action

inputs.description: Controller action values, one per robot control dimension; the fake pads or trims to its width
inputs.name: action.values

actions.name: step

actions.description: Reset the simulated world to a scenario start state and return the initial observation. When a seed is supplied the endpoint records it in the receipt; otherwise the endpoint's declared default seed applies.

inputs.description: Index of the initial state, as reset(init_index=seed) reads it
inputs.name: seed

actions.name: reset_world

facts.text: VAB is a self-contained-YAML manipulation benchmark: one file per task supplies arena, robot, objects, initial states, success predicate and language
The documented quick start loads a task YAML with load_task, builds the environment with task.make_env(), calls reset(init_index=i), then step(action) and unpacks a four-tuple
The README calls the 50 initial states of a single-arm task seeds and loops over task.n_inits
The README states the observation contract: images are uint8[H,W,3] per camera, proprio is joint_pos[7], joint_vel[7], eef_pos[3], eef_quat[4] (xyzw) and gripper_qpos[2]
Success is returned only as info['success']; a multi-target predicate also surfaces completion_rate in 0..1 and delivery_progress()
The README example sets cameras agentview and robot0_eye_in_hand at camera_height 128 and camera_width 128
The README lists 62 tasks across 8 suites under tasks/
load_task resolves the YAML path, parses it with yaml.safe_load and validates it into a Task
Task.make_env dispatches to VABBimanualEnv when the YAML lists two robots and to VABEnv otherwise
VABEnv subclasses robosuite's SingleArmEnv
VABEnv selects renderer='mujoco' and passes the task's control frequency, horizon and camera names to robosuite
reset(init_index) defaults to task.default_init_index, applies that initial state and returns the filtered observation
reset raises IndexError when init_index is not below len(task.inits)
step unwraps robosuite's (obs, reward, done, info), adds success, language and completion_rate to info, and returns the filtered observation
The filtered observation has exactly the images and proprio keys; images are keyed by the task camera names and proprio holds joint_pos, joint_vel, eef_pos, eef_quat and gripper_qpos
language_instruction returns task.language and action_dim returns robots[0].action_dim
delivery_progress returns a (delivered, total) pair or None, and reward is 1.0 on success and 0.0 otherwise
The bimanual class is VABBimanualEnv, a TwoArmEnv subclass
VABBimanualEnv.action_dim is the sum of both robots' action dimensions
The task YAML example names robot panda with controller OSC_POSE and the two cameras at 128 x 128
The smoke test asserts the observation keys are exactly images and proprio, asserts the agentview shape from the task's camera height and width, and asserts success and language in info
requirements.txt pins robosuite 1.4.0 with numpy, opencv-python, matplotlib, pyyaml and pydantic
setup.py declares python_requires >=3.8 and name libero

determinism.notes: the reset input is the initial-state index (the README calls the initial states seeds), and VABEnv applies the matching YAML pose, so one init index and one action sequence repeat on the same environment; the environment exposes no random-number seed, so cap.world.seed.v1 is not bound and the package makes no claim about robosuite's internal physics randomness

gaps: the fake backend is not robosuite/MuJoCo: it keeps a placeholder joint vector, applies a first-order motion of it and resolves no contact, controller, actuator or free-joint dynamics; it never evaluates the YAML success predicate and always reports success False

the fake returns 2 x 2 x 3 pixel frames per camera, while the real task YAMLs set camera_height 128 and camera_width 128 (README.md:93-94); the fake's proprio arrays use the documented lengths but Python floats instead of float32 numpy arrays
the fake was never compared with the upstream environment: robosuite 1.4.0, MuJoCo, numpy and pyyaml were not installed where the gate ran
only one single-arm VABEnv is served; the card's VABBimanualEnv and load_task entry symbols are not bound, and no task YAML is loaded (the environment's task is not configured)
the environment's control step is the default control_freq 20 Hz (env.py:56), i.e. 50 ms; there is no wall-clock pacing (realtime_factor 0)
rendering is not served as a capability: images arrive inside the observation, but cap.world.* binds no render class and no artifact store
snapshot and restore are not offered: the environment exposes no get_state/set_state
no physical robot is modelled and nothing was validated against hardware

safe_state.description: the simulation stops advancing: no step or reset is accepted after an e-stop until mhs.safety.reset clears the latch; the observation, reward and tick stay readable
